module.title: Ability: Can, Could, Be Able To

grammar_concept.title: Ability: Can, Could and Be Able To
grammar_concept.rule: Use 'can' for present ability, 'could' for general ability in the past, and 'be able to' (in any tense, including 'will be able to' for the future) whenever 'can'/'could' isn't grammatically possible.
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: "Can" and "could" are modal verbs — they never change form (no -s, no -ed, no "to" before the next verb) and have no future form. "Be able to" behaves like a normal verb and can fill the gaps that "can"/"could" leave, especially in the future.
grammar_concept.example: I can swim. When I was a child, I could run very fast. Next year, she will be able to drive.
grammar_concept.example_translation: Eu sei nadar. Quando era criança, eu conseguia correr muito depressa. No próximo ano, ela vai poder conduzir.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: Falantes de português tendem a tentar usar "can" em qualquer tempo verbal, por transferência direta de "poder"/"conseguir" — dizem "I will can drive" em vez de "I will be able to drive", porque "can" não tem forma de futuro nem se combina com outro modal.
grammar_concept.correction: Nunca use "can" no futuro ou depois de outro modal — use "will be able to". Para o passado, "could" serve para capacidade geral; para uma conquista específica, prefira "was/were able to".
grammar_concept.real_world_example: In a CV: "I am able to work under pressure and can speak three languages."

vocabulary.definition_en: to have the ability or opportunity to do something
example_sentences: She wasn't able to come to the meeting yesterday.

vocabulary.definition_en: to succeed in doing something difficult
example_sentences: We managed to finish the project on time.

vocabulary.definition_en: in a stressful situation with high demands

exercises.prompt: Complete: When I was young, I ___ swim very well.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "can" no passado ("I can swim when I was young") é o erro mais comum aqui.

exercises.prompt: Complete: Next year, she ___ drive to work.
exercises.explanation: "Can" não existe no futuro — usa-se "will be able to".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: "Will can" é um erro muito comum, por tradução direta de "vai poder".

correct_answer: to succeed in doing something difficult
exercises.explanation: "Manage to" implica sucesso apesar da dificuldade, não apenas a intenção.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. Could Marco swim when he was five?
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "When Marco was five, he couldn't swim at all."
exercises.transcript: When Marco was five, he couldn't swim at all. Now he's able to swim very well.

exercises.prompt: Read: "Ana wasn't able to attend the interview on Monday, but she managed to reschedule it for Friday." When is Ana's interview now?
exercises.explanation: O texto diz diretamente que ela "reschedule[d] it for Friday".

exercises.prompt: Translate to English: "Eu não consegui terminar o relatório ontem, mas vou conseguir terminá-lo amanhã."
correct_answer: I wasn't able to finish the report yesterday, but I will be able to finish it tomorrow.
I couldn't finish the report yesterday, but I will be able to finish it tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: No passado, "não consegui" pode ser "wasn't able to" ou "couldn't"; no futuro, só "will be able to" é possível — "will can" não existe.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Traduzir "vou conseguir" como "I will can" é o erro mais comum nesta frase.

steps.content: "Can" is usually weak and fast in a sentence — /kən/, almost swallowed — but "can't" is stressed and clear — /kænt/. Listen for that stress difference, not just the final "t", to tell them apart in natural speech.

steps.prompt: Talk about something you couldn't do as a child but can do now, and something you hope you'll be able to do in the future.
Write 4 sentences about your abilities: one with "can", one with "could", one with "was/were able to", and one with "will be able to".
